unit: L7 본문 — Seasonal Festivals Around the World
parts: 중2 L7 본문 — Seasonal Festivals Around the World
sentences: Fallas Festival in Valencia, Spain People in Valencia celebrate the coming of spring with the Fallas festival.
This festival takes place from March 15 to 19.
During the festival, people enjoy parades and fireworks.
The stars of the festival are fallas, giant wooden statues.
You can find hundreds of them all over the city.
Surprisingly, the fallas are burned on the last day of the festival.
Burning them symbolizes saying goodbye to old things and hello to a new start.
Midsummer Festival in Sweden Winter in Sweden is long and dark, so the people there especially welcome summer.
To celebrate the longest day of the year, they have a special festival.
They call it the Midsummer festival.
The festival starts on the Friday evening between June 19 and 25 and ends on the Sunday.
During the festival, people decorate a tall pole with flowers and green leaves and enjoy traditional dances around it.
Because the sun hardly sets at this time of year in Sweden, people can enjoy the festival all night long.
Day of the Dead Festival in Mexico Many Mexicans believe that once a year dead people come back home to meet their family and friends.
They call this day the Day of the Dead.
To welcome dead people, Mexicans hold a festival on November 1 and 2.
They believe it is important to remember dead people.
So, people set up altars in their homes and have big parties in cemeteries.
In some areas, people dress up like skeletons and hold big parades.
Fur Rondy Festival in Alaska, USA At the end of February, people in Alaska hold the Fur Rondy festival, one of the biggest winter festivals in the world.
During this festival, visitors can enjoy various winter sports and Alaskan traditional games.
They can also enjoy many special events such as the Running of the Reindeer.
People who participate in this race wear fun costumes and try to run faster than reindeer.
Is it possible to do so?
Not really, but it doesn’t matter.
Everyone is just having fun!

items.statement_ko: 스페인 발렌시아 사람들은 Fallas 축제로 봄이 오는 것을 기념한다.
items.why_ko: 1번 문장에서 봄이 오는 것을 Fallas 축제로 축하한다고 했다.
_evidence_text: Fallas Festival in Valencia, Spain People in Valencia celebrate the coming of spring with the Fallas festival.
items.statement_en: In Valencia, Spain, people welcome the arrival of spring through the Fallas festival.

items.statement_ko: Fallas 축제는 3월 5일부터 9일까지 열린다.
_evidence_text: This festival takes place from March 15 to 19.
items.statement_en: The Fallas festival runs from March 5 to March 9.

items.statement_ko: Fallas 축제 기간에 퍼레이드는 열리지만 불꽃놀이는 하지 않는다.
_evidence_text: During the festival, people enjoy parades and fireworks.
items.statement_en: At the Fallas festival, there are parades but no fireworks.

items.statement_ko: 축제의 주인공인 fallas는 거대한 돌 조각상이다.
items.why_ko: 돌이 아니라 나무로 만든(wooden) 거대한 조각상이다.
_evidence_text: The stars of the festival are fallas, giant wooden statues.
items.statement_en: The fallas, the main stars of the festival, are huge statues made of stone.

items.statement_ko: 도시 곳곳에서 수백 개의 fallas를 볼 수 있다.
items.why_ko: 5번 문장에서 도시 전역에 수백 개가 있다고 했다.
_evidence_text: You can find hundreds of them all over the city.
items.statement_en: Hundreds of fallas can be seen in many places around the city.

items.statement_ko: fallas는 축제 첫날에 불태워진다.
items.why_ko: 첫날이 아니라 축제 마지막 날에 태운다.
_evidence_text: Surprisingly, the fallas are burned on the last day of the festival.
items.statement_en: The fallas are set on fire on the first day of the festival.

items.statement_ko: fallas를 태우는 것은 옛것과 작별하고 새 출발을 맞이한다는 의미이다.
items.why_ko: 7번 문장에 그 상징적 의미가 그대로 나온다.
_evidence_text: Burning them symbolizes saying goodbye to old things and hello to a new start.
items.statement_en: Burning the fallas means saying goodbye to old things and welcoming a fresh start.

items.statement_ko: 스웨덴은 겨울이 길고 어두워서 사람들이 여름을 특별히 반긴다.
_evidence_text: Midsummer Festival in Sweden Winter in Sweden is long and dark, so the people there especially welcome summer.
items.statement_en: Because winter is long and dark in Sweden, people there are especially glad when summer comes.

items.statement_ko: 스웨덴 사람들은 일 년 중 가장 짧은 날을 기념하기 위해 축제를 연다.
items.why_ko: 가장 짧은 날이 아니라 가장 긴 날을 기념한다.
_evidence_text: To celebrate the longest day of the year, they have a special festival.
items.statement_en: Swedish people hold their festival to celebrate the shortest day of the year.

items.statement_ko: 스웨덴 사람들은 그 축제를 Midsummer 축제라고 부른다.
_evidence_text: They call it the Midsummer festival.
items.statement_en: Swedish people give this festival the name Midsummer festival.

items.statement_ko: Midsummer 축제는 6월 19일과 25일 사이의 토요일 아침에 시작한다.
_evidence_text: The festival starts on the Friday evening between June 19 and 25 and ends on the Sunday.
items.statement_en: The Midsummer festival begins on the Saturday morning between June 19 and 25.

items.statement_ko: 사람들은 높은 기둥을 꽃과 푸른 잎으로 장식하고 그 주위에서 전통 춤을 춘다.
_evidence_text: During the festival, people decorate a tall pole with flowers and green leaves and enjoy traditional dances around it.
items.statement_en: People put flowers and green leaves on a tall pole and dance traditional dances around it.

items.statement_ko: 이 시기 스웨덴에서는 해가 거의 지지 않아 밤새 축제를 즐길 수 있다.
_evidence_text: Because the sun hardly sets at this time of year in Sweden, people can enjoy the festival all night long.
items.statement_en: At this time of year the sun almost never goes down in Sweden, so people can enjoy the festival through the whole night.

items.statement_ko: 많은 멕시코인은 한 달에 한 번 죽은 사람들이 집으로 돌아온다고 믿는다.
items.why_ko: 한 달에 한 번이 아니라 일 년에 한 번이다.
_evidence_text: Day of the Dead Festival in Mexico Many Mexicans believe that once a year dead people come back home to meet their family and friends.
items.statement_en: Many Mexicans believe that dead people return home once a month.

items.statement_ko: 멕시코인들은 죽은 사람이 돌아오는 그날을 Day of the Dead라고 부른다.
_evidence_text: They call this day the Day of the Dead.
items.statement_en: Mexicans call the day when dead people come back the Day of the Dead.

items.statement_ko: Day of the Dead 축제는 10월 31일 하루 동안 열린다.
_evidence_text: To welcome dead people, Mexicans hold a festival on November 1 and 2.
items.statement_en: The Day of the Dead festival is held for only one day, on October 31.

items.statement_ko: 멕시코인들은 죽은 사람들을 기억하는 것이 중요하다고 믿는다.
_evidence_text: They believe it is important to remember dead people.
items.statement_en: Mexicans think that remembering people who have died matters a lot.

items.statement_ko: 사람들은 묘지에 제단을 세우고 집에서 큰 파티를 연다.
items.why_ko: 제단은 집에 세우고, 큰 파티는 묘지에서 연다.
_evidence_text: So, people set up altars in their homes and have big parties in cemeteries.
items.statement_en: People build altars in cemeteries and hold big parties in their homes.

items.statement_ko: 일부 지역에서는 사람들이 해골처럼 분장하고 큰 퍼레이드를 벌인다.
_evidence_text: In some areas, people dress up like skeletons and hold big parades.
items.statement_en: In some places, people put on skeleton costumes and have big parades.

items.statement_ko: 알래스카의 Fur Rondy 축제는 12월 말에 열린다.
_evidence_text: Fur Rondy Festival in Alaska, USA At the end of February, people in Alaska hold the Fur Rondy festival, one of the biggest winter festivals in the world.
items.statement_en: The Fur Rondy festival in Alaska takes place at the end of December.

items.statement_ko: Fur Rondy 축제에서 방문객들은 다양한 겨울 스포츠와 알래스카 전통 놀이를 즐길 수 있다.
_evidence_text: During this festival, visitors can enjoy various winter sports and Alaskan traditional games.
items.statement_en: Visitors to the Fur Rondy festival can try many kinds of winter sports and traditional Alaskan games.

items.statement_ko: Running of the Reindeer는 Fur Rondy 축제의 특별 행사 중 하나이다.
_evidence_text: They can also enjoy many special events such as the Running of the Reindeer.
items.statement_en: The Running of the Reindeer is one of the special events at the Fur Rondy festival.

items.statement_ko: 이 경주에 참가하는 사람들은 순록을 타고 달린다.
items.why_ko: 순록을 타는 것이 아니라 재미있는 옷을 입고 순록보다 빨리 달리려 한다.
_evidence_text: People who participate in this race wear fun costumes and try to run faster than reindeer.
items.statement_en: People who join this race ride on the backs of reindeer.

items.statement_ko: 글쓴이는 순록보다 빨리 달리는 것이 가능한지 질문을 던진다.
_evidence_text: Is it possible to do so?
items.statement_en: The writer asks whether running faster than a reindeer can really be done.

items.statement_ko: 대부분의 참가자는 실제로 순록보다 빨리 달릴 수 있다.
items.why_ko: 사실상 불가능하지만 그것은 중요하지 않다고 했다.
_evidence_text: Not really, but it doesn’t matter.
items.statement_en: Most of the runners are actually able to beat the reindeer in speed.

items.statement_ko: 참가자들은 모두 그저 즐거운 시간을 보낸다.
_evidence_text: Everyone is just having fun!
items.statement_en: All the people there are simply enjoying themselves.
